**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** (Reviewed at the safety-floor tier; no UI change, so no hand check is needed beyond the usual look at a drawn neck in the simulation if wanted.)

**What looks good**
- Fail-safe by construction. A neck is used only if it `agrees` with the tool numbers, runs contiguously from the flute top to the stickout, is finite, has at most `MAX_BANDS` bands, and is nowhere wider than the stated shank (`neck.rs` `neck_bands`, `HolderStack::shank_bands`; `NeckBands::fits` in `Cutter::judged`). Any failure returns the exact old `(flute_len, shank_len, shank_radius)` band, so it can only over-report.
- I looked for a collision that stops being flagged and found none. The neck is narrower than the shank only over the drawn outline's own conservative bands (`SpunProfile::bands`, which never undercut the outline). Gaps and agreement slack are filled at the shank radius, merging only grows a band, and a holder body beside the shank widens the neck band it stands beside. `tool_body::judged`/`enclose` only ever grows `shank_d`, and a grown shank with a neck wider than the stored one falls back or is widened to the body. Judging the neck against the stored record and then re-fitting it to the judged record is sound.
- Every law that reads the shank band now reads the same one: c/c3 (reach), c2, d2 (stack_span), the posed sweep, the mesh sweep and the solid-law atoms. The picture and the checks share the seam. The leftover generator-side cylinders (drill reach, probe stylus, multiaxis avoid) stay conservative and are named for #842.
- A drawn neck enters the op stamp (bytes only when a neck exists), so a stale toolpath is not reused. A no-neck tool is bit-identical (pinned).
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` in new code. Provenance lines present, decisions file included, no build.rs / .github / scripts / Cargo / process-file / snapshot / CHANGELOG changes. Body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #852`.

**Local results (merged with upstream/main - already up to date, no conflicts)**
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| camcraft-tools lib (incl. 6 new `neck_tests`) | 62 passed |
| camcraft-sim lib + 16 gate-mapped suites | all ok (0 failed) |
| camcraft-motion `real_tip`, `solid_law` | ok |
| camcraft-app lib + `tool_neck_laws`, `sim_tool_body`, `tool_body*`, `tool_cutter_profile`, `tool_spun_profile`, `fixtures`, `fixture_route`, `fixture_ux`, `c_axis_fixture`, `posting`, `stock_stamp`, `carried_verify`, `project_roundtrip`, `probe_reach` | all ok (0 failed) |
| clippy `-p tools -p sim -p motion -p app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |
| remaining quick app suites, ui suites | not re-run by me (PR reports them green; the diff does not touch ui) |

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- `crates/sim/src/verify/probe.rs` ~line 62: the new doc line `/// Its drawn neck (#852) ...` sits after `#[must_use]` and is glued onto `with_body`'s doc block out of order; move it above the attribute.
- The pinning tests prove the neck clears steel and undo restores the strike, but no test shows steel *inside* the neck radius (e.g. a block 3.5 mm off a Ø8 neck) is still convicted. Worth adding as a follow-up negative pin.
- Still not exercised, as the PR says: an end-to-end generation where law (c) acquits a deep necked cut.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 54ed3fe799ea27dec6e3a2693bac31b0021a2c53 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

This is a maintainer-side review at the safety tier. I built it together with #1012, which is stacked on it: one worktree on #1012's head (0ea437f9, which contains this PR's 54ed3fe7), trial-merged with `main` e0cb0049. The merge was clean. This review adds to the author's earlier review and replaces nothing.

### What looks good
- **One seam.** Every stack law reads the shank through `HolderStack::shank_bands` / `Cutter::shank_bands`: laws c and c3 (`reach.rs:45`), c2 (`laws.rs:160`), d2 (`stack_span.rs:148`), the posed sweep (`posed_steel.rs:124`), the mesh law (`mesh_steel.rs:77`) and the solid law's atoms (`probe.rs:193`). The simulation meridian (`sim_tool_body::with_neck`) reads the same bands, so what is drawn is what is judged.
- **Direction of every verdict change: looser only where it is true to the steel.**
  - Upright: a neck no wider than the cutter now stands in the flutes' kerf, the same rule main applies to any band within the cutter radius.
  - A neck between the cutter and shank radius is judged at its own radius.
  - The fixture, mesh and posed laws sweep the neck's real radius.
  - Nothing became stricter. A holder body standing beside the shank widens the neck band next to it (`neck.rs`, `beside`), so the neck is never narrower than the body around it.
- **#843 / #903 tilt rule survives.** I wrote my own scratch test with the `tool_body_bands` harness; it was not committed or pushed. The tool: Ø8 cutter, neck r 3.5 from 8 to 20, shank r 6 from 20 to 38.
  - Tilted 30° toward a part wall with the neck in the part and the shank above the top: law (c) convicts (`ShankHit{part:true}`).
  - Tilted with the neck's column clear and the r 6 shank leaning into the wall: convicts, the same as main's cylinder.
  - Upright, wall 5 mm off the axis, only the neck level with it: clean, where main's cylinder convicts. That is the intended and correct loosening.
  - A neck r 4.5 (wider than the cutter): convicts with the wall 4.2 mm off the axis and is clean at 4.7 mm.
- **Degenerate necks fall back to the cylinder, never to nothing.** Each of these gives `shank_bands` equal to the cylinder and `Cutter.neck == None`: a band wider than the shank, a zero-length band, NaN or infinite numbers, a negative radius, a neck that stops short of the stickout, a neck that starts late.
- No drawn cutter, or a drawn cutter with no neck: the bands are bit-identical and the stamp bytes are unchanged (`tool_cutter::digest` writes only when a neck exists). No golden moved.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. No new dependency. Provenance lines are present. Components stay in `schema.rs`. No snapshot PNG changes.

### Local results (merged with main e0cb0049, Windows, debug)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --tests` | 40 binaries, 327 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-tools` (incl. `neck::tests` 6, `cutter_fit::tests` 4) | 69 passed |
| app `tool_neck_laws` | 4 passed |
| app `tool_body_bands` | 13 passed |
| app `tool_body_judged` | 8 passed |
| app `sim_tool_body` | 7 passed |
| app `tool_cutter_profile` | 5 passed |
| app `tool_spun_profile` | 7 passed |
| app `tool_cutter_params` | 3 passed |
| app `verify` | 21 passed (2 ignored) |
| app `golden_cl` | 25 passed |
| app `conformance` | 6 passed |
| app `commands_undo` | 30 passed |
| app `project_roundtrip` | 71 passed |
| app `mcp` | 13 passed |
| motion `solid_law` | 6 passed |
| `camcraft-ui --lib` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 536 passed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Not run: the release-lane `--ignored` heavy tests and the snapshot lane.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (non-blocking)
1. `HolderStack::shank_bands` accepts a band with `r == 0.0` (`ok` is `>= 0`), and law (c) skips `band_r <= 0` as excused. `neck_bands` cannot produce one today, because a spun outline refuses interior points on the axis (`spun.rs:136`). Still, `b.r > 0.0` in `fits` would make the seam hold on its own.
2. `probe.rs`, `Cutter::with_body`: the new doc line `/// Its drawn neck (#852) ...` sits after `#[must_use]`, which splits the doc comment around the attribute. It is cosmetic.
3. Drill reach, the probe stylus and multi-axis tilt avoidance stay on the stated cylinder. That is conservative and is left to #842, as the PR says.
4. File length: `operation/job.rs` crosses the 400-line line (397 to 401); `generate.rs` (3289) and `schema.rs` grow by 2 lines each.
5. Merge order: this PR first, then #1012, which is stacked on it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
